statement: Create a schedule of building components for a chosen category and phase, then choose its fields, filters, sorting and grouping, formatting and appearance in a tabbed properties dialog.
superiority: Edit values in the schedule and see geometry update with unlimited rows and instant filtering.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Totals and grouping are options inside the Sorting/Grouping and Formatting tabs, not part of the creation step. Acceptance sketch: Door schedule rows equal the number of doors and area totals match element sums.

statement: Add fields from the category and define calculated values by formula over parameters.
superiority: Allow richer expressions, units-aware formulas and reusable calculated fields.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Calculated value width times height equals the stored area.

statement: Add a calculated percentage field that reports a field's share of its total, either overall or within one of the schedule's grouping fields.
superiority: Show share-of-total graphically in the schedule.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Percentage option documented on the Calculated Values page (Of and By fields); By can reference a grouping field, default is whole schedule. Acceptance sketch: Percentages sum to 100 within rounding.

statement: Limit schedule rows with up to eight case-sensitive field conditions that must all be satisfied, including filtering by the sheet on which the schedule is placed.
superiority: Support OR and nested groups.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Page states up to 8 filters, all must pass, and a sheet-based filter option. Acceptance sketch: Filter returns only matching rows.

statement: Sort rows by a primary field and further 'then by' fields, add group headers, footers with counts or totals and blank lines, and choose to itemize every instance or collapse identical rows.

source.ref: Sort and Group Fields in a Schedule

superiority: Collapsible groups with persisted state and sticky headers.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Maximum number of sort levels is not stated in the page I read, so the 'four fields' limit is dropped. Acceptance sketch: Grouped totals equal the sum of the rows in each group.

statement: Format fields, headings, units, alignment, hidden columns and conditional formatting.
superiority: Conditional rules with colours and icons.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Hidden column not shown but still sorts.

statement: Control schedule grid lines, outline, a blank row before data, row striping, title and header display, and the text types used for title, headings and body.

source.ref: Change the Appearance of a Schedule

superiority: Reusable schedule themes shared across projects.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Page lists grid lines, outline, blank row, stripe rows, title/header visibility and text types; banding is 'Stripe Rows' (session-only); column width is not on this page. Acceptance sketch: Settings persist when the schedule is placed on a sheet.

statement: Create a material takeoff schedule that lists the materials or sub-components of a family with quantities such as area, volume and cost, reported per material rather than per instance.
superiority: Update live from the model and export to a bill of quantities.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Page describes sub-components or materials with quantities and costs; per-layer detail for walls is implied by material-based reporting, with noted approximations in volumes. Acceptance sketch: Takeoff area for a layered wall equals the layer area from geometry.

statement: Create a sheet list that serves as a document-set table of contents using chosen fields, user-defined fields and optional placeholder sheets, with the usual filter, sort and format tabs.
superiority: Add a custom sheet naming rule and bulk create sheets.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Revision status is not a built-in column on this page; fields are user-selected. Acceptance sketch: List shows all sheets.

statement: Create a note block schedule that lists the instances of a chosen generic annotation family with selected parameters such as description.
superiority: Sync note text from a spec library.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: A note block lists placed generic annotation instances by family, not keyed notes placed by element. Acceptance sketch: Count equals placed notes.

statement: Create a view list of all project views by default, choosing fields and using the filter tab to omit views, shown in the Project Browser and drawing area.
superiority: Edit view parameters in bulk.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Template and sheet placement are available only as selectable fields; default includes all views. Acceptance sketch: List includes all views.

statement: A keynote legend lists keynote key values and text and can be filtered by keynote division or limited to the keynotes visible in views on the sheet where it is placed.

source.ref: Filter a Keynote Legend by Sheet

superiority: Interactive legend where clicking a key highlights its elements.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Filtering by sheet and by key value are two separate options. Acceptance sketch: Legend lists exactly the keys placed in the view.

statement: Place a schedule on a sheet by dragging it from the Project Browser, edit it in place, and split it into segments with a break control to fit the sheet.

source.ref: Split a Schedule on a Sheet

superiority: Responsive schedule layout.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Placement is documented in Add a Schedule to a Sheet; splitting uses the Z-break control with adjustable segment rows. Acceptance sketch: Split schedule shows continuation.

statement: For schedules of rooms, spaces, duct systems, piping systems or electrical circuits, embed a second schedule that lists member components beneath each parent row.
superiority: Support arbitrary cross-category joins with explicit keys.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Embedding only applies to rooms, spaces, duct, piping systems and circuits, not arbitrary schedule-in-schedule nesting. Acceptance sketch: Embedded rows relate to the parent row by the join field.

statement: Add project or shared parameters as custom schedule fields, noting that categories lacking a selected shared parameter drop out of a multi-category schedule.
superiority: Link to external data.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Cross-project reuse of shared parameters is not described on this page; use of shared parameters as fields is. Acceptance sketch: Shared parameter appears.

statement: Create room schedules and space schedules by choosing the Rooms or Spaces category, selecting fields such as finishes and custom room parameters, and sorting or filtering by them.
superiority: Live reconciliation with area plans.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Beginner workflow page for rooms; spaces covered by Creating a Space Schedule. Department as a built-in parameter not verified on the page. Acceptance sketch: Room area column sums to total area.

statement: Export a schedule view to a delimited text file with options for column header rows, group header/footer export, field delimiter and text qualifier.
superiority: Two-way sync with spreadsheet.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Adds documented export options; schedules on sheets can also export to CAD and CSV. Acceptance sketch: Exported rows equal schedule rows.

statement: Update parameter values from a spreadsheet through a plug-in or Dynamo script.

source.doc: https://help.autodesk.com/view/RVT/2027/ENU/ ; Revit 2027 Help topic: Schedule: Import from Spreadsheet (ecosystem)

superiority: Native two-way spreadsheet binding.
notes: UNVERIFIED 2026-11-14: Searched help (find.py --all) for schedule import, Excel and spreadsheet topics plus RevitDynamo topics; no Revit 2027 page documents importing schedule values from a spreadsheet, and Dynamo Excel nodes are not in the indexed RevitDynamo pages. Likely an add-in/Dynamo ecosystem feature, not a core command. Acceptance sketch: Values updated match sheet.

statement: Set a schedule's Phase and Phase Filter in the Properties palette so it quantifies only elements in the chosen phase status, such as new or demolished work.

source.ref: Apply a Phase to a Schedule

superiority: Compare phases in one view.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Page documents Phase and Phase Filter parameters on the schedule. Acceptance sketch: Phase filtered rows exclude demolished.

statement: Set the units format of numeric fields, calculate column totals, and show min/max or grand totals in summary schedules.
superiority: Reconcile display and stored values.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Subtotals appear only in summary schedules (itemize cleared); grand totals are a Sorting/Grouping option. Acceptance sketch: Total honours unit format.

statement: Tags read instance or type parameters via label definitions in the tag family.
superiority: Compose labels from a visual list.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-11-14 Acceptance sketch: Label shows type parameter.

statement: In a tag family's Edit Label dialog, build a label from parameters with per-parameter prefix, suffix, spaces, sample value, forced line break and wrap-between-parameters-only options.
superiority: Live tag family preview with real data.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Separator is expressed through spaces/prefix/suffix; sample value, break and wrap options confirmed. Acceptance sketch: Label text matches parameter.

statement: Keynotes come from a tab-delimited text file of keys, descriptions and parent/child hierarchy, editable in a spreadsheet or text editor and reloaded from the keynote settings.
superiority: Edit keynotes inside the app with versioning.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Edits apply after reopening the project or reloading the file. Acceptance sketch: Table loads and keys resolve.

statement: Number door and window Mark values with numbering templates that partition by a parameter such as the room a door opens into and format sequence letters or numbers with prefixes, or fall back to sequential placement-order marks.
superiority: Renumber on room change with a log of what changed.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Room-based numbering is a Numbering template (Manage tab); default marks are sequential by placement (Create Sequential Tags for Doors or Windows). Acceptance sketch: Marks are unique and follow the configured rule after edits.

statement: Create a multi-category schedule or material takeoff that lists elements from many categories together, using fields common to them such as shared parameters.

source.ref: Expanded Category List for Multi-Category Schedules and Material Take-offs

superiority: Filter and group across categories with mixed units normalised.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-11-14: Multi-category schedules documented in What's New 2022 page; shared-parameter filtering behaviour is from Create a Schedule or Quantity. Acceptance sketch: Rows from all chosen categories appear and totals match the per-category sums.

statement: Filter schedule rows by whether a parameter is or is not tied to a chosen global parameter.

source.ref: Filter a Schedule by Global Parameter Association

superiority: Show the association graph beside the schedule.
notes: ADDED 2026-11-14: feature found documented in Revit 2027 help during the verification pass; not in the original register Acceptance sketch: Associate a parameter to a global, then filter a schedule for associated and unassociated elements.

statement: Combine two or more parameters into one read-only schedule column using a chosen separator, prefixes and suffixes.
superiority: Allow combined fields to be used for sorting and filtering.
notes: ADDED 2026-11-14: feature found documented in Revit 2027 help during the verification pass; not in the original register Acceptance sketch: Combine door width, height and thickness with 'x' and verify the single column text.

statement: Schedules can include image fields (instance, type or rebar shape images) managed through an images dialog so schedule rows show pictures.
superiority: Automatic thumbnails generated from the family geometry.
notes: ADDED 2026-11-14: feature found documented in Revit 2027 help during the verification pass; not in the original register Acceptance sketch: Assign a type image to a furniture type and confirm it appears in a schedule column.

statement: Insert schedule views saved in another project, preserving formatting and custom fields, or save a schedule view to a new project file.

source.ref: Use a Schedule in Another Model

superiority: Link schedules live rather than copying them once.
notes: ADDED 2026-11-14: feature found documented in Revit 2027 help during the verification pass; not in the original register Acceptance sketch: Save a schedule to a new file, insert it into another project, and compare fields and formatting.
